key_concepts: Vertebrates are animals with a backbone made of vertebrae
The backbone protects the spinal cord and the skull protects the brain
Vertebrates have an internal endoskeleton with muscles attached to bones
Ectothermic vertebrates have body temperature that changes with the environment
Endothermic vertebrates keep a constant body temperature
Vertebrates are classified into fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals
Fish live in water, have fins and scales, breathe with gills, and are cold-blooded
Amphibians begin life in water with gills and later develop lungs and legs for land
Reptiles are cold-blooded, have dry scales, lay eggs on land, and breathe with lungs
Birds are warm-blooded, have feathers and wings, and lay hard-shelled eggs
Mammals are warm-blooded, have fur or hair, and feed young with milk from mammary glands
Vertebrates have blood circulation, gas exchange through lungs or gills, and a brain-based
